chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Baseer who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever judges in a matter involving two dirhams by other than what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed, is a disbeliever in Allah the Great.'

key_terms.العظيم: The Great, the Magnificent — a divine epithet emphasizing the majesty of the God whose law is being violated
key_terms.حكم: To judge, to rule, to adjudicate — the root h-k-m encompasses both political authority and legal adjudication
key_terms.درهمين: Two dirhams — a coin of small monetary value, used rhetorically to mean even the most trivial matter
key_terms.كافر: Disbeliever — one who rejects or conceals divine truth; here applied to judges who set aside divine law
key_terms.ما أنزل الله: What Allah has revealed — referring to the Quran and the divinely-guided Sunnah

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about a judge who rules by other than what Allah revealed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issued a sweeping ruling that even the smallest monetary dispute, here symbolized by two dirhams — a trivial sum — must be adjudicated according to divine revelation. The Imam's use of the specific term 'kafir' (disbeliever) for judges who deviate from God's law reflects the gravity of usurping divine legislative authority. This teaching was directed at a context where political rulers and their appointed judges were applying non-Islamic standards, and Abu Baseer, a trusted close companion, transmits the Imam's uncompromising stance on judicial integrity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Humran, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who judges regarding two Dirhams by other than what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed, so he is a disbeliever with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Magnificent’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Humran from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
One who issues judgment on the basis of something other than what Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has sent is in denial of the existence of Allah, the most Great.’”
